mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Single path election: (A) if the destination state is an Apostille Convention member, notarize the certificate by a Hong Kong notary public, then obtain an Apostille from the High Court of the HKSAR; (B) if the destination state is not an Apostille Convention member, notarize by a Hong Kong notary public and then submit for consular legalization at that State's consulate or embassy in Hong Kong. Paths (A) and (B) are parallel and mutually exclusive; never combine them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Current Standing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Single path election: (A) for Apostille Convention members, notarize the certificate then apply to the High Court of the HKSAR for an Apostille; (B) for non-members, notarize the certificate then obtain consular legalization from the destination State's consulate or embassy in Hong Kong. Use only one path; apostille and consular legalization are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Incorporation and Bank Account Opening

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If executed in mainland China: notarization by an official PRC notary office followed, for Apostille Convention member destinations, by an Apostille from the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or an authorized provincial foreign affairs office; for non-member destinations, use consular legalization by the destination State's consulate. If executed in Hong Kong: notarization by a Hong Kong notary public followed by HKSAR High Court Apostille (member states) or destination consulate consular legalization (non-member states). One path only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: CN_JV_LTD and registered Corporate Service Provider with Companies Registry, HKSAR
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Single path election: (A) for Hague Apostille states, notarize the certified copy by a Hong Kong notary public and obtain an Apostille from the High Court of the HKSAR; (B) for non-Hague states, notarize the certified copy and then submit to the destination State's consular office for consular legalization. The two methods are mutually exclusive and must never be applied in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank maintaining the corporate account (e.g., HSBC, Standard Chartered, or Bank of China Hong Kong)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If issued by a Hong Kong bank, use: (A) Hong Kong notarization plus HKSAR High Court Apostille for Hague Apostille member states; or (B) Hong Kong notarization plus consular legalization by the destination State for non-member states. If issued by a mainland Chinese bank, use: (A) PRC notarization plus Apostille by PRC MFA or authorized provincial foreign affairs office for Hague states; or (B) PRC notarization plus consular legalization for non-member states. Select exactly one path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Single path election: (A) notarization by a Hong Kong notary public followed by HKSAR High Court Apostille for Apostille Convention member states; (B) notarization by a Hong Kong notary public followed by consular legalization at the destination State's consulate or embassy in Hong Kong for non-member states. ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding, identify and verify each legal entity layer (Hong Kong company, PRC WFOE, and ultimate beneficial owners) using certified identity documents and independent registry data. Screen all named shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, and UBOs against the HK Commercial and Economic Bureau sanctions lists, HK Customs and Excise enforcement notices, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UK and EU consolidated lists, and PRC dishonest-judgment-debtor lists. For any PEP, assess source of wealth and funds, require senior management approval, apply enhanced due diligence, and re-screen monthly for 36 months post-termination. Adverse hits require immediate suspicious transaction report to the HK Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) e-Registry and Name Search Service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Hong Kong name may be English only, Chinese only, or bilingual. English names must use Roman letters and end in 'Limited'; Chinese names must be in Traditional Chinese characters and end in '有限公司'; no statutory phonetic transliteration is required, but the Chinese name must not create confusion with an existing registered name. For the PRC WFOE parent, the four-tier naming rule applies: administrative division + unique trade name + industry description + limited-liability organizational form. English foreign names used as translations are not protected by the Chinese name registration and must be separately cleared.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Registry refuses a name, obtain the written refusal grounds and submit a revised name application within 14 days. If the applicant disputes the decision, file a formal review letter with the Registrar of Companies setting out the legal basis for registrability; after refusal at review, appeal to the Administrative Appeals Board under the Administrative Appeals Board Ordinance (Cap. 570) within 28 days. For the mainland WFOE parent, simultaneously petition the local municipal market supervision authority and, if necessary, SAMR.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is legally sufficient for Companies Registry registration only if it is a genuine street address and service accepts statutory mail; however, Inland Revenue Department and licensed banks will not accept a shared commercial mailbox or virtual-only suite for this low-code SaaS business because they require evidence of local management, lease in the company name, utility accounts, and employee presence. A virtual office is therefore operationally unusable for opening a bank account, obtaining a Stripe/Paddle merchant account, or substantiating Hong Kong tax residence; a full physical office or dedicated serviced office with company signage is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection checklist: (i) company name displayed at registered office; (ii) original lease or service agreement in company name; (iii) utility bill matching the registered address; (iv) employment and payroll records for HK staff; (v) board meeting minutes maintained at the registered office; (vi) statutory records and significant-controllers register available. Quantified risk: 5% annual probability for a standard low-risk software company with no tax residence claim; 25% probability if the company applies for an HK tax-resident certificate or claims the PRC-HK DTA benefit without visible substance; 40% probability if a bank referral or substantial no-code SaaS subscription turnover triggers an Inland Revenue Department audit.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), sections 67, 68, 115 and 116; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), section 5; the 'Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture' designation reflects shareholder ownership composition, and the entity is formed as a Hong Kong private company limited by shares. PRC Sino-Foreign Joint Venture Law does not apply in the Hong Kong SAR.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, 14/F, Queensway Government Offices, 66 Queensway, Hong Kong; electronic filing through the e-Registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Form NNC1 (Application for Incorporation of a Local Company) together with the adopted Articles of Association, submitted through the Companies Registry e-Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong private companies limited by shares have no statutory minimum paid-up share capital requirement. The subscribers may declare a nominal share capital as low as one ordinary share, and no blocked escrow account or capital deposit certification is required. The PRC joint-venture parent may internally agree on capitalization, but the Companies Registry does not mandate proof of payment for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] (INCORPORATED IN HONG KONG UNDER THE COMPANIES ORDINANCE CAP. 622)

At a meeting of the directors of the company duly convened and held at the registered office on [date], with the requisite quorum present, the directors unanimously resolved as follows:

1. INCORPORATION RATIFICATION. RESOLVED that the incorporation of the company, the allotment of shares to the subscribers, and the adoption of the Articles of Association as submitted to the Companies Registry be, and the same are hereby, ratified and approved in all respects.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED that the registered office of the company shall be situated at [address] and that this office shall be the place where the statutory registers, minute book, and corporate seal shall be kept and made available for inspection as required by sections 115 and 119 of the Companies Ordinance.

3. CAPITAL AND SHARE ISSUANCE. RESOLVED that the initial share capital set out in the incorporation form, comprising no par value ordinary shares, be subscribed and deemed issued to the subscribers and shareholders as recorded in the register of members, and that the directors may issue further shares in accordance with the Articles.

4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED that the directors be and are hereby authorized to open, operate, and close bank accounts with such licensed banks in Hong Kong as they may select; that any two authorized directors, or one director and the company secretary, may sign checks, mandates, contract documents, and electronic banking directions; that such banks may rely upon written mandates approved by the board and shall incur no liability to the company for acting in accordance with such instructions.

5. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS AND GOVERNANCE. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed as director and [Name] as company secretary, and that the directors, jointly and severally, are authorized to execute all documents, file all returns, and appear before the Companies Registry and Inland Revenue Department for the purpose of completing statutory registrations and compliance.

6. COMPLIANCE AND INDUSTRIAL LICENSING. RESOLVED that, as the company is engaged solely in no-code software platform development and related digital services, no physical industrial, environmental, or civil defense permit is required; the directors shall nonetheless maintain the Business Registration Certificate and comply with any applicable professional and data protection legislation.

7. EXECUTION AND RECORDING. RESOLVED that this resolution be recorded in the minutes and signed by the chairman, and that copies be certified for banking and contractual counterparties.

These resolutions shall take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Search and Availability Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry - Cyber Search Centre and e-Registry (Hong Kong SAR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-incorporation name search via the Companies Registry Cyber Search Centre to ascertain that the proposed company name is not identical or too similar to an existing Hong Kong company name under section 100 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). Confirm the exact English name and, if desired, the Chinese name for the no-code software platform business. Verify availability of the name against trade mark and intellectual property records where practicable. Prepare the intended business description as ISIC 6201 visual web template and low-code web application builder for the corporate record. Input the proposed shareholders' percentage equity holdings and director details into the preliminary application worksheet, and obtain any required parent-company board authorization letter for the Chinese joint venture shareholder before formal submission.
required_dossiers: Proposed English company name and optional Chinese name
Copy of passport or identity card of each proposed shareholder and director
Business activity description (ISIC 6201 no-code website builder)
Corporate shareholder certificate of incorporation and board resolution (if any shareholder is an entity)
Authorisation letter from the PRC parent company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected because it is the same as or nearly resembles an existing name, the applicant may obtain a written consent of the existing company, or revise the company name and immediately resubmit the name reservation through the e-Registry. No additional filing fee is incurred for a single corrected submission made within the same business day, but a new application processing clock will start.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of Incorporation Form NNC1 and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the e-Registry portal, complete Incorporation Form NNC1, setting out the company name, registered office address, initial share capital, first shareholders, first director(s) and company secretary. Attach the executed Articles of Association and any certified identification documents. For the PRC corporate shareholder, append the certified board resolution and notarized copies of its business licence. Declare that the company will conduct no-code software development, visual web template design and related information technology services, and will not engage in physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing activities. Pay the incorporation fee and business registration levy using the e-Registry payment gateway. Upon successful submission, print the transaction receipt and acknowledge the electronic statutory declaration as made under the Companies Ordinance.
required_dossiers: Completed and executed Form NNC1
Articles of Association subscribed by every subscriber
Certified identification copies of all proposed directors and secretary
Registered office address proof (lease or landlord consent)
Corporate shareholder resolutions and business licence copies
Payment transaction receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry treats the application as suspended for any deficiency, the authorised applicant receives a notice describing the required correction. The applicant must cure the defect within 21 days by updated PDF, revised Form NNC1 or supplementary statutory declaration. A failure to respond within 21 days results in the application being deemed withdrawn; the same filing may be resubmitted with a new fee and processing period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry and Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Companies Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation, and the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department issues the Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance. Verify that all details match the approved NNC1, including the company name, business nature, date of commencement and expiry date. Retain these certificates in the corporate minute book and use them for opening corporate bank accounts and payment processor applications. If the Business Registration Certificate is not delivered automatically within the SLA, make a written application to the Business Registration Office with the Certificate of Incorporation and pay the statutory levy. This step does not create an industrial or environmental licence because the entity is purely digital.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by Companies Registry
Business Registration Certificate issued by IRD
Approved Articles of Association
Fee payment receipts
Executed first director and company secretary consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Certificate is not issued, present the Certificate of Incorporation and transaction receipt to the Business Registration Office and request immediate issuance. Any late-issuance penalty is remitted if the company proves electronic filing on the original date. For certificate inaccuracies, file a written correction request with supporting identity and proof of business nature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopting First Board Resolution and Establishing Corporate Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and adopt the pro-forma first board resolution as set out in the incorporation_legal_framework object, covering share allotment, registered office confirmation, banking authorization and statutory officer appointments. Since the entity is a no-code website builder with ISIC 6201, record a formal statement that no environmental impact assessment or civil defense fire permit is applicable, because the company has no physical plant. Execute bank mandate forms in the absence of the Hong Kong bank officer, and have each authorised signatory sign specimen signatures. Open the corporate bank account using the incorporation documents and maintain statutory registers at the registered office. If shares are allotted, file the Return of Allotment with the Companies Registry within one month.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
Executed pro-forma first board resolution
Bank account mandate and signature cards
Register of members, directors and company secretary
Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate
Return of Allotment Form NNC5 (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any statutory filing after board adoption is rejected, correct the form by following the Companies Registry guidance notice and resubmit within 14 days. For bank rejection due to incomplete mandates, re-execute the account opening documents with full board approval and verify that the beneficial ownership declaration matches the registered shareholders.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - ISIC 6201 is a pure digital service; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing licence is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no physical project, no EIA registration or full report required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams from no-code software operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no industrial premises; only the general Business Registration Certificate and any landlord fire safety certifications under the Buildings Ordinance apply to the leased office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - the competent tax authority for the Hong Kong jurisdiction in this formation, not the State Taxation Administration of Mainland China. Online electronic portal: eTAX (Electronic Services for Tax) at www.gov.hk/etax. Customs administration is separately handled by the Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity or joint-venture limited company operating in Hong Kong obtains its statutory taxpayer identity through the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310). After incorporating at the Companies Registry under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), or after registering as a registered non-Hong Kong company, the entity must apply to the Business Registration Office of the IRD using the prescribed application form within one month of commencing business. The IRD issues a Business Registration Certificate (BRC) bearing a Business Registration Number (BRN); the BRN is the Hong Kong taxpayer identification number and must be quoted in Profits Tax returns, employer returns, and customs trade declarations. Foreign non-resident entities that do not carry on business in Hong Kong and do not derive Hong Kong-source income are not obliged to obtain a BRN solely because they are foreign entities. Non-resident persons who become chargeable to Hong Kong Profits Tax may be issued an IRD tax file number for assessment purposes. Applications can be submitted through the IRD eTAX portal, by post, or in person at the Business Registration Office; the prescribed registration fee and levy must be paid. The territorial-source principle is applied separately under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), but this is a scope rule, not a registration election.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Hong Kong does not provide check-the-box elections, pass-through entity elections, or hybrid-mismatch elections. Entity classification follows the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) and company law; profits tax is imposed at the entity level on profits with a Hong Kong source.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Not Applicable - Hong Kong imposes no VAT, no GST, and no general sales and use tax. Certain goods are subject to duty under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (Cap. 109), and certain documents are subject to stamp duty under the Stamp Duty Ordinance (Cap. 117), but these are not general indirect taxes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - there is no VAT/GST registration threshold or economic-turnover rule because Hong Kong has no VAT/G

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) / State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for PRC-side capital account controls; Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the de facto central banking and clearing authority for the Hong Kong SAR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is conditionally convertible: current-account payments may be settled freely by authorized banks after documentary verification, while capital-account outbound investment requires prior ODI filing with MOFCOM/NDRC and SAFE registration. The Hong Kong dollar is fully convertible under the HKMA's linked exchange rate system, with no surrender or approval requirement for ordinary corporate payments. The critical bottleneck is the PRC parent's injection of equity capital into the HK JV: funds cannot be remitted until the parent obtains its Certificate of Overseas Investment Filing from MOFCOM/NDRC and completes SAFE registration with a qualified PRC bank. Upon receipt in Hong Kong, the JV must treat the funds as shareholder capital and support the inward remittance with a board resolution, share allotment, and Companies Registry filings. Dividend repatriation from HK to the PRC parent is unrestricted at the HK side but will be characterized as Chinese tax-resident dividend income and may attract withholding tax under the arrangement between mainland China and Hong Kong; adequate economic substance and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation must be maintained to avoid recharacterization. A separate capital escrow ledger is recommended to segregate injected capital from operating revenue.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The Hong Kong JV is outside PRC surrender rules. Any PRC trading subsidiary that holds export foreign-exchange receipts must repatriate the proceeds into a domestic foreign-exchange account within 30 days from receipt, and the mandatory conversion ratio is zero because enterprises may choose to retain the currency or sell it to a PRC bank as permitted by SAFE. The HK JV itself can keep receivables freely in HKD/USD.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for low-value SaaS collections but Low as the primary banking layer. Hong Kong's Banking Ordinance restricts deposit-taking and clearing settlement to authorized institutions, so offshore EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Currenxie) can act only as money-service operators or SVF licensees and cannot issue commercial letters of credit, provide RMB NDFs, open CHATS settlement accounts at HKMA, or serve as the custodian of injected share capital. The JV may use Stripe/Paddle as merchant-of-record rails for subscription billing, with settlement flows swept automatically to a tier-1 bank account. All capital injections, trade disbursements, and FX hedges must be executed at a licensed commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The JV must anticipate an in-person interview. HKMA's AMLO expects banks to verify controllers and source of wealth; HSBC and BoCHK generally require at least one statutory director and the UBO to appear in branch with original IDs. Remote consular proxy opening is occasionally accepted for low-risk software companies if the director executes a power of attorney before a notary and the consulate apostilles the certified corporate documents, but it is not guaranteed. The budget should include travel to Hong Kong for the PRC-nominated director and the AML compliance officer, plus a 10-day onboarding lead time.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial capital injection from a PRC parent to a newly incorporated HK JV with no previous trading history may be flagged as wealth-structuring or disguised cross-border money movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ODI filing receipt and registration certificate from SAFE, NDRC and MOFCOM approvals (where applicable), PRC parent's business license and 3-year audited financial statements, source-of-funds bank statements, board resolution approving the injection, HK Companies Registry incorporation certificate, and a chronological flow-of-funds diagram with purpose and source of each remittance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The declared no-code website builder activity is digital and intangible, creating uncertainty over whether end customers, subscription revenues, or software licenses can be independently verified.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SaaS product contracts and standard terms of service, privacy policy, acceptable-use policy, customer KYC/sanctions screening process, IP registration or code deposit proof, data protection impact assessment, third-party security audit, and a statement of business substance including employee headcount, office lease, and operational management in Hong Kong.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of Stripe and Paddle as principal payment gateways blurs the identity of underlying payers and can trigger correspondent-bank de-risking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed payment processor agreements, PCI DSS compliance attestation, API integration documents, monthly settlement and payout reports, transaction-level export file sampling, end-customer relationship list, chargeback/refund policies, and a money-laundering risk assessment prepared by an external compliance consultant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shared registered address, corporate secretary, or nominee shareholder arrangements by a HK formation agent may be treated as shell-company symptoms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory UBO filing with the HK Companies Registry, trustee/nominee declarations and consent letters, corporate service provider engagement letter, employee contracts and MPF records, HK office lease or sublease, utility bills, board meeting minutes, and a list of bank relationships to prove physical substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital must flow from the PRC parent's SAFE-qualified bank under the approved ODI quota using a wire with purpose code 'Overseas Direct Investment - Equity'. The remittance should be received in the HK JV's Capital Escrow Account at a designated tier-1 bank; after receipt, the bank will issue an inward remittance credit advice, and the JV should promptly file the share allotment (Form SC1) with the Companies Registry and issue shares to the parent. For amounts exceeding the HKMA large-value threshold, use CHATS or SWIFT MT103; do not split transactions to avoid declaration thresholds. Capital verification is evidenced by the bank's credit advice, share certificate register, and safe accounting; if the PRC parent requests a capital verification report, a Hong Kong certified public accountant can certify against the bank statements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for routine supplier and vendor settlement in USD/EUR/HKD with invoice and reference fields tagged to the underlying purchase order. For large-value procurement of hardware/cloud infrastructure, use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit, confirmed by a Hong Kong bank, with transport and inspection documents attached. Documentary collections are acceptable for low-risk, high-volume trade flows where the counterparty's bank status is established. All outbound disbursements above HKD 100,000 should be processed through a tier-1 bank with anti-fraud call-back verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward FX contracts (up to 12 months tenor) between HKD and USD, and USD and CNH, limited to underlying trade/investment exposure.
Non-deliverable RMB forwards (NDFs) on CNH/CNY to hedge PRC parent remittance or procurement invoiced in RMB, provided an underlying exposure is documented.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps between HKD and USD fixed/floating for debt-service payment matching.
FX options (put/call) if approved by the HKMA-recognized bank treasury within a non-speculative risk limit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 42nd day immediately following the anniversary of the company's incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers escalating penalties: HKD 870 if over 42 days but not more than 3 months; HKD 1,740 if over 3 months but not more than 6 months; HKD 2,610 if over 6 months but not more than 9 months; HKD 3,480 if over 9 months. Continued default may result in prosecution and administrative strike-off of the company under Section 746 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, on or before the expiry date of the current Business Registration Certificate, generally no later than 1 month before the registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts a late fee of HKD 300 per month (or part thereof) for each month the certificate remains unrenewed, up to a maximum of HKD 1,800, in addition to the full annual fee. Failure to renew may lead to prosecution under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) with fines up to HKD 5,000 and up to 6 months' imprisonment; the business is not lawfully allowed to operate without a valid certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Profit Tax Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the issue date of the return, which is normally issued on the first working day of April; an automatic extension of 2 months is allowed if a Hong Kong tax representative is appointed, and further extensions may be granted depending on the financial year end (e.g., up to 15 June for year-ended 31 December companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Without reasonable excuse, late filing exposes the company to a fine of up to HKD 10,000 for the first offence and up to HKD 50,000 for subsequent offences, plus an additional assessed amount of up to 10% of the tax undercharged. The IRD may issue a best-of-judgement assessment under Section 59 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, increasing the tax liability and exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Employer's Return Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the issue date of Form BIR56A, typically issued on the first working day of April; must be filed together with IR56B statements for all employees for the preceding year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the Employer's Return without reasonable excuse attracts penalties under the Inland Revenue Ordinance: a fine from HKD 1,000 to HKD 10,000, and on conviction a fine up to HKD 10,000 plus an additional fine of HKD 1,000 for each unclaimed employee IR56B form; further daily penalties may apply for continued failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Presentation of Audited Financial Statements, Directors' Report, and Auditor's Report to Members at Annual General Meeting (or by Written Resolution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders (and, if specifically requested, the Companies Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a private company, within 9 months after the end of each accounting reference period; for a public company, within 4 months. The period is prescribed by Section 612 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to hold or dispense with the annual general meeting within the statutory period are liable to a fine of HKD 300,000 and a daily default fine of HKD 2,000 for continued contravention. Failure to present audited financial statements may result in similar penalties and contempt of court proceedings; administrative strike-off may also be triggered for persistent non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Section 403 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), every company incorporated in Hong Kong, unless dormant, must appoint a certified public accountant (practising) to audit its consolidated or individual financial statements, and the auditor's report must be prepared in accordance with Hong Kong Standards on Auditing. No quantitative size-based exemption exists; hence, irrespective of balance sheet totals, turnover or headcount, statutory audit is compulsory for all active companies. For simplified reporting only, the Companies Ordinance defines a 'small private company' as meeting at least two of the following: annual revenue not exceeding HKD 100 million; gross assets not exceeding HKD 100 million; and total number of employees not exceeding 100. Such companies may prepare simplified financial statements but are still subject to a full statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA). Eligible small- and medium-sized entities may alternatively apply the HKFRS for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE), which is a simplified but still fully compliant framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing. Instead, every company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) at its registered office or another prescribed location, as required by the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) Part 17. The SCR must contain the full name, residential or service address, identity document details, nationality, nature and extent of control, and the date of appointment or cessation of significance for every significant controller. The company must take reasonable steps to identify its significant controllers and must update the register within 7 days of receiving any notification of change. The annual return (NAR1) requires the company to declare the physical address where the SCR is kept. There is no discrete 30-day reporting window for shareholding transfers, but any transfer that changes the status of a person as a significant controller must be recorded in the SCR within 7 days. Failure to maintain the SCR or to keep it up to date is a criminal offence punishable by a fine of HKD 25,000 and an additional daily fine of HKD 700 for continued non-compliance.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory 25% headline CIT may be reduced to 15% for a qualifying High and New Technology Enterprise, to an effective 5% for a small low-profit enterprise (taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million, employees not exceeding 300, total assets not exceeding RMB 50 million, regime effective until 2027), to 10% for a National Key Software Enterprise, and to a two-year CIT exemption followed by a three-year 50% reduction for a qualifying software enterprise in the no-code / low-code ISIC 6201 business. A 100% additional super deduction is available for eligible R&D expenses. Technology transfer income is exempt up to RMB 5 million and taxed at 50% of the normal rate on the excess. Hainan Free Trade Port encouraged industries may access a 15% CIT rate, and qualifying Western Development enterprises likewise enjoy a 15% rate. Loss carryforward is generally 5 years, extended to 10 years for qualifying high-technology and small-medium technology enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return of the People's Republic of China (Form A, 2017 Revision) and supplementary schedules, filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax portal of the in-charge tax authority where the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is registered.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement return with quarterly provisional prepayments; quarterly returns are due within 15 days after each quarter-end and the annual Form A is due within 5 months after fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed and final tax paid by May 31 of the following year for a calendar-year taxpayer. Quarterly provisional CIT prepayments must be filed within 15 days after the close of each quarter. Withholding returns for outbound dividends, interest, and royalties must be filed at the time each payment is made to the non-resident payee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue from sale of website-builder subscriptions, low-code web application tools, no-code template licenses, maintenance, support, and hosting-related services recognized under PRC accounting standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all revenue settled through Stripe, Paddle, or other payment rails even if collected by an offshore merchant of record; the JV is a Chinese tax resident and is taxed on worldwide income. Convert foreign-currency receipts to RMB at the applicable tax declaration exchange rate. Do not exclude revenue routed to a Hong Kong bank account absent a valid legal and tax reason; any unreported offshore collection will be treated as concealed income and recharacterized as an unauthorized diversion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs directly related to revenue: cloud infrastructure, third-party software licenses, template developer compensation, subcontracting, server hosting, bandwidth, and customer support cost.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party cloud, hosting, and service charges paid to an HK affiliate must be supported by written contracts, invoices, bank records, and evidence of actual service and benefit. Unsupported or non-arm's-length HK charges will be disallowed and may be recharacterized as a constructive dividend to the HK shareholder, triggering 10% withholding tax (or 5% under the DTA if treaty conditions are met).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, and administrative expenses: personnel, marketing, rent, office, professional fees, travel, entertainment, and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees and headquarters cost allocations from the HK parent are deductible only if there is a genuine service agreement, the service was actually performed, the JV benefited, and no double-charging exists. A straight commission or profit-stripping management fee without underlying activity will be challenged as lacking economic substance. Non-deductible entertainment expenses and excessive administrative allocations must be added back on the CIT adjustment schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and non-operating expenses, including government grants, compensation, penalties, donations, asset retirement, and foreign-exchange gains or losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Equity injections from the HK parent are not taxable income to the extent of registered capital, but advances labeled equity while creating debt-like, guaranteed returns may be reclassified as distributed profits or taxable interest. Government subsidies for software or R&D are taxable unless expressly exempt by law. Do not offset HK shareholder subvention payments against Chinese taxable income absent a valid equity or lending relationship.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss carryforward after accounting profit is reconciled through revenue, expense, and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box captures all add-backs and deductions: thin-capitalization interest disallowance, transfer-pricing adjustments, non-deductible related-party fees, and denied entertainment expenses. The JV must attach the annual related-party transaction declaration forms. Any transfer-pricing adjustment asserted by SAT will begin here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after utilization of qualifying prior-year tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use carryforward losses from prior year CIT returns; general carryforward is 5 years, 10 years for qualifying High/New Technology enterprises. There is no loss carryback. If the JV claims loss offsets while demonstrating no employees, no premises, or no business substance, tax authorities may invoke the General Anti-Abuse Rule and recalculate taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT rate and initially calculated CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% standard rate; 15% if the JV holds a valid High/New Technology Enterprise certificate; effective 5% if it qualifies as a small low-profit enterprise; or 10% for national key software enterprises. The no-code software and template business must meet technical, R&D-expense, and software-revenue tests to claim software enterprise holiday benefits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, tax reduction/exemption, other credits, and final net CIT payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the JV has foreign-source taxable income, it may claim a foreign tax credit for income taxes paid abroad, limited to the Chinese CIT payable on that foreign-source income. Hong Kong profits tax on HK-source income can be credited if supported by an HK tax assessment or tax payment certificate. Attach detailed foreign tax credit schedules and maintain all documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit after tax, profit-distribution resolution, and non-resident dividend withholding tax obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is not a CIT line but it is mandatory for the JV before repatriating profits. If the JV distributes dividends to its HK parent, Chinese non-resident withholding income tax applies at a 10% statutory rate, reduced to 5% under the Mainland-HK DTA only if the HK recipient is the beneficial owner that directly holds at least 25% of the JV capital and satisfies the holding-period and substance requirements. The JV must file the withholding return, pay the WHT, and obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from the HK Inland Revenue Department before remitting the dividend.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form A or quarterly CIT returns triggers an administrative fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 plus daily late-payment interest of 0.05% on unpaid tax. Underreporting tax by false return or concealment triggers a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63. Failure to withhold Chinese WHT on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties triggers a penalty of 50% to 300% of the unwithheld amount under Article 69. Tax evasion exceeding RMB 50,000 and 10% of the tax due is a criminal tax-fraud threshold under Criminal Law Article 201, carrying imprisonment up to three years, and three to seven years for especially large evasions, together with fines and forced recovery. Legal representatives and directors may also face exit bans and tax blacklisting for unpaid tax liabilities.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding income tax on dividends distributed by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise under CIT Law Article 37 and its Implementing Regulations; reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA if the HK beneficial owner is a company directly holding at least 25% of the JV capital for the 12-month period preceding the dividend declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the 5% DTA rate, the JV and HK parent must: (1) obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Inland Revenue Department for the distribution year; (2) submit the non-resident enterprise treaty-benefit declaration or application to the Chinese in-charge tax authority; (3) prove beneficial ownership with board minutes, share registry, HK substantive presence, the JV distribution resolution, and evidence that the HK recipient is not a conduit or shell; (4) file the WHT return and pay the reduced rate at the time of the dividend remittance; and (5) retain all treaty-benefit and beneficial-ownership evidence for at least 10 years under SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9. Beneficial ownership is denied for contractual or shell arrangements whose only purpose is treaty access.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties and interest paid to a non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in China is 10% for each category. Under the Mainland-HK DTA, the maximum WHT for interest is 7% and for royalties is 7% where the HK payee is the beneficial owner; the protocol may provide special treatment for equipment-related royalties, so the current Arrangement must be reviewed. Related-party interest in excess of the thin-capitalization debt-to-equity ceilings (2:1 for general enterprises, 5:1 for financial institutions) is non-deductible and can be recharacterized as a constructive dividend, attracting the 10% or 5% dividend WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under SAT Announcement No. 42 of 2016, the Local File is mandatory when annual related-party transactions in tangible property, services, or other categories reach RMB 200 million, and when related-party transactions of intangible property or financial assets reach RMB 100 million. The Master File is required for MNE groups with annual aggregate related-party transactions reaching RMB 1 billion. An annual Related Party Transaction Declaration is required whenever any related-party transactions occur, even below the documentation thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies a substance-over-form doctrine through CIT Law Article 47, SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9, and the General Anti-Abuse Rule. The JV must be the economic owner of the no-code website-builder IP and must perform its core income-generating activities (CIGA) in China: software development, customer contracting, product support, revenue recognition, and risk management. The Hong Kong parent, to enjoy DTA benefits and any HK tax-exemption claim, must satisfy Hong Kong Economic Substance Requirements applicable to relevant activities; a pure equity-holding entity needs reduced substance, but for financing, licensing, or trading activities it must have sufficient employees, premises, board meetings, and operating expenditures in Hong Kong.
